en: The Sutra of the Names of Eight Buddhas, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was together with a great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as a great assembly of ten thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the Mahāyāna.
At that time, the World-Honored One, surrounded before and behind by immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of beings, was preaching the Dharma for them.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra rose from his seat amidst the great assembly, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"I have a doubt and now wish to pose a question; I only pray that the Tathāgata, out of compassion for sentient beings, will explain it to me.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra, saying: "Good son!
"According to what you ask, if there is any doubt in your mind, I shall analyze and explain it for you.
At that time, Śāriputra, having received the Buddha’s approval and permission to resolve his web of doubts, was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Are there currently Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, in the worlds of the ten directions, who, by virtue of their past vows, constantly preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings?

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to recite and uphold the names of these Tathāgatas—whether reading them, hearing them, or transcribing them—and by the merit resulting from this, they attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, without deficiency or diminution, reaching the unsurpassed, right, and true path and swiftly attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! O son of good family!"

The sublime eloquence with which you have questioned me will bring vast benefit to immeasurable sentient beings in future ages; out of compassion and pity for all devas and humans, you have been able to inquire of the Tathāgata regarding such profound meanings as these.
"Therefore, listen now with close attention and receive it well; reflect upon it thoroughly, and I shall explain it to you in detail.
Śāriputra said, "So be it, World-Honored One!"
"I wish to hear it with joy.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra, saying:
"O son of good family!

To the east, passing from here through worlds as numerous as the sands of one Ganges River, there is a buddha-field named Hard to Subdue (*Durjayā*). In that land dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Renowned for the Merit of Excellent Discourse (*Suvyākhyātābhigīta-guṇa*), who at present is preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for a great assembly.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east from here, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of two Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field named Unobstructed. In that land dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Indra-lakṣaṇa-dhvaja-tārārāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who at this very moment is also preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of three Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field named Priyaṃkara. In that land dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Samantaprabhā-guṇavyūha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who even now is preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east from here, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of four Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field named Universal Entry. In that land dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Well-Fought, Invincible, and Transcendent Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who at present also teaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma to a great assembly."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of five Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field named Pure Assembly (Vimalasaṃcaya). In that land dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Universal Merit Radiance Adornment Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who at present also expounds the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of six Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field named Avyādhipati. In that land there is a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Anāvaraṇabhaiṣajyataru-guṇakīrti Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who even now dwells there, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east of here, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of seven Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field named Filled with Pervasive Fragrance. In that land dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Padmaprabhūta Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who even now resides there, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

To the east from here, passing through worlds as numerous as the sands of eight Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field named *Ghoṣadattāloka*. In that land dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Ratnapadmasupratiṣṭhitaśālarājā Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who at present also teaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly."

“Śāriputra! These Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, possess such pure and stainless Buddha-fields, free from the five turbidities and devoid of the five desires. The sentient beings therein have no minds of flattery, crookedness, or hypocrisy, nor do they engage in sensual conduct, and there are no women.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if good sons and good daughters hear the names of those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and having heard them, are able to personally uphold, read, recite, and practice them, and further proclaim and explain them to others— then it is impossible for those good sons and good daughters to fall into the three evil realms;
this applies except in the case of the five heinous crimes, slandering the True Dharma, or reviling the Noble Ones."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If good men or good women hear the names of those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and having heard them, are able to personally uphold, recite, and practice them, and further proclaim and expound them for others—such persons, until they reach Bodhi, in every place of birth throughout that interval, will always possess the five supernormal powers, and moreover attain various dhāraṇīs; their six sense organs will be complete without any deficiency, and they will always experience joy with the hairs on their bodies curling to the right."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If good men and good women hear the names of these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and having heard them, are able to personally uphold, recite, and practice them, and further proclaim and explain them to others—wherever those sentient beings may dwell, officials and wicked bandits shall find no opportunity to harm them; fire cannot burn them, water cannot sweep them away, and evil dragons or evil snakes cannot inflict poison upon them.

Whether walking or staying, it is impossible for lions, tigers, wolves, bears, brown bears, jackals, leopards, yakṣas, rākṣasas, various malevolent spirits and ghosts, kumbhāṇḍas, and other humans or non-humans to cause them alarm or fear, except in the case of calamities resulting from past karma."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if there is a woman who can grow weary of her female body and, with focused mindfulness and single-minded devotion, receives, maintains, reads, and recites these names of the World-Honored Buddhas, and furthermore explains and elucidates them for others— should she, after the end of her life, again receive a female body, such a thing is impossible."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If there are good men or good women who, during the stillness of night, can recite the names of these Buddhas, such sentient beings will find that all the meritorious deeds they perform in this present world are swiftly accomplished and increase day by day, free from all obstacles."
At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke these verses:
"If there are sentient beings Who can uphold the names of these Buddhas,
They shall all abandon the evil realms And swiftly be reborn in auspicious places."
Constantly before all Buddhas, one eternally hears the preaching of the wondrous Dharma;
having beheld the Unsurpassed Honored One, one makes offerings according to one's heart.
By reciting and upholding the Buddha’s name, one transcends billions of kalpas.
All afflictions shall swiftly be extinguished as one attains Bodhi.
If a person for seven full days can recite these names of the Buddhas,
they will immediately obtain the pure eye and be able to see all the Buddhas.
If there are those who hear the Buddha’s name and are able to recite and uphold it,
wherever they are born, they will always be honored by others.
With the marks and signs of physical excellence and a handsome form, they will always be born into families of merit and happiness.
Practicing a joyful mind and great equanimity, being intelligent and heedful—
if there are women who, upon hearing this name of the Buddha,
recite it themselves or speak of it to others, their merit shall be immeasurable.
When their life here has come to an end, they will surely cast off the female form and receive a male body;
in birth after birth, their faculties shall always be sharp.
Because they recite and uphold the Buddha’s name, throughout many hundreds of billions of kalpas,
Their breath shall always be fragrant, Constantly like the scent of sandalwood.
If one can recite and uphold The names of these various great seers,
With a subtle mind and without negligence, [one shall attain such results].
By reciting and upholding the names of the Buddhas, parents, brothers,
and all other kinsmen shall never experience any further suffering.
By reciting and upholding the names of the Buddhas, all Māras Pāpīyas—
The hosts of dark and gloomy attendants can never create obstacles;
poisonous venom cannot harm them, nor can swords, staves, fire, and the like;
officials, wicked bandits, and thieves—none of these can cause them injury.
By reciting and upholding the names of the Buddhas, for thousands of billions of kalpas,
one shall always be born from precious lotus flowers, endowed with majestic marks and supernormal powers;
constantly dwelling in the midst of space, pervading inconceivable lands.
Beholding the various Buddha-lands, those pure realms within the *kṣetras*,
having realized the unsurpassed path, they universally serve as a place of refuge for all diverse beings— gods and worldlings alike.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Venerable Śāriputra, along with the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sutra of the Names of Eight Buddhas
